chunks: And from him, from Abdullah al-Qaddah, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace:
That Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who bowed (in prayer) and did not recite the glorifications (subhanallah) out of forgetfulness, so he said: 'His prayer is complete.'

key_terms.رَكَعَ: He bowed (performed the ruku' position in prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does forgetting to recite the glorifications in the bowing position invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes that forgetting the recommended glorifications (tasbihat) during ruku’ does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia principle that omissions of sunnah acts due to forgetfulness do not break the prayer's validity. This ruling underscores the distinction between obligatory pillars (arkan) and recommended acts, providing practical ease for worshippers in their daily devotions.
